problem: Waypoint predictors for VLN-CE use complex RGB-D architectures and often output waypoints that are in obstacles or not linearly reachable. Zero-shot LLM navigators also keep only step-wise history, so they lose track of explored regions, loop, and cannot plan backtracking for error correction.
motivation: RGB/depth carry much irrelevant information that obscures traversability, while the waypoint space is a 2D radial grid. Prompts that record only visit order give the MLLM no spatial connectivity or explicit visited/unvisited status, so it gets stuck and cannot recover from mistakes.
key_idea: Predict linearly reachable waypoints from an abstract binary obstacle map (built from depth gradients) with a light transformer, then feed the MLLM a dynamically updated topological graph plus explicit visit information so it explores and backtracks.
insight: Both the graph and the visit information matter: removing TopoGraph drops SR from 46 to 37 and removing VisitInfo drops it to 40 (R2R-CE, 300-episode ablation). The obstacle-map predictor also beats DC-VLN's predictor under the same prompting (SR 46 vs 42, collisions 3.85 vs 9.98), which suggests RGB semantics are unnecessary for waypoint prediction. With the same GPT-5-mini API, the full pipeline beats an adapted AO-Planner (SR 46 vs 33).
method: Obstacle map construction: panoramic depth is converted to a point cloud and projected onto the 120x12 radial grid (3° x 0.25 m, up to 3 m). Per-cell max height is computed, then elevation gradients along each radial direction are taken, and cells whose gradient exceeds a threshold are marked as obstacles. This handles stairs and slopes better than a fixed height threshold.

Lightweight waypoint predictor: the obstacle map is the sole input to a 2-layer transformer encoder with a classification head that outputs logits over the 120x12 grid. It is supervised with ground-truth waypoint heatmaps and trained for 30 epochs.
Linear-reachability masking: for each direction, logits beyond the first obstacle are masked out, then NMS selects the top-K waypoints, matching the turn-then-move low-level motion.

Dynamic topological graph: following ETPNav, nodes are visited or unvisited. Waypoints are not regenerated at visited nodes. Waypoints near existing nodes reuse the node's ID and location, and near-duplicate waypoints are merged (MergingModule).

VisitInfo and TopoGraph prompting: the prompt contains instruction, image history, trajectory IDs, textualized graph connectivity (MapGPT style), visit status of the action options, supplementary images of unvisited nodes, and action options with 4-view images. Predicted waypoints are projected onto the RGB images. The MLLM outputs Thought and Action.
Exploration and local planning: the MLLM prioritizes unvisited nodes, and on a detected error it uses graph connectivity to backtrack one or multiple steps and re-explore.

setting.backbone: GPT-5-mini (frozen) as navigator + 2-layer transformer-encoder waypoint predictor (trained)
setting.training_data: Only the waypoint predictor is trained, on the DC-VLN ground-truth MP3D connectivity graph (train split). The MLLM is zero-shot.
setting.action_space: low-level Move-forward 0.25 m, Turn-left/right 15°, Stop, executed via waypoint selection (turn-then-move)

results: Zero-shot SOTA on R2R-CE (SR 41, SPL 25.4, NE 6.12) beating SmartWay (SR 29, SPL 22.0) and AO-Planner (SR 25). On RxR-CE it gets SR 35.7 vs AO-Planner 22.4. It is still well below supervised ETPNav (R2R-CE SR 57; RxR-CE SR 54.8). The waypoint predictor reaches the best %Open (90.18) and Avg_Score (1.56).
limitations: Still a clear gap to the best supervised method (ETPNav) on SR, SPL and nDTW, and SPL is low relative to SR, so paths are long.
Evaluation is on a 300-episode subset for RxR-CE and ablations, and relies on the closed GPT-5-mini API, which limits reproducibility and cost.
Waypoint predictor is limited to 3 m local range and needs training on the MP3D graph.
